title: Three Workers Die After Inhaling Toxic Gas at Tata's Hosur iPhone Plant
excerpt: The contract workers were cleaning a nano-filtration tank at the Hosur plant's effluent treatment plant late on Monday. Apple, Tata Electronics and Tamil Nadu authorities will investigate, as officials say proper safety measures were not in place.
body:
• Three contract workers died late on Monday after inhaling toxic gas while cleaning a nano-filtration feed tank at Tata Electronics' iPhone components plant in Hosur, Tamil Nadu.
  • The effluent treatment plant where the incident happened is operated by Nalco Water, an Ecolab subsidiary; the workers were engaged by one of Nalco's sub-contractors.
  • Apple, Tata Electronics and Tamil Nadu authorities will investigate the deaths, according to officials and sources cited by Reuters.
  • iPhone production was not affected because the plant was closed for the Diwali festival this week.

Three contract workers have died after inhaling toxic gas during maintenance work at a Tata Electronics factory that makes components for Apple iPhones in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, according to Inc42's report of the incident and Reuters reporting carried by The Business Standard. The deaths occurred late on Monday, November 9, while the workers were carrying out cleaning and maintenance work at the facility's effluent treatment plant.

What Happened at the Tank

The workers were cleaning a nano-filtration feed tank at the effluent treatment plant, which is operated by Nalco Water, a subsidiary of the US-based Ecolab. Citing The New Indian Express, Inc42 reported that one worker fainted after looking inside the tank and inhaling gas, and that the other two entered the tank to check on him and also collapsed from asphyxiation. All three were declared dead on arrival at hospital.

Krishnagiri district official Dinesh Kumar said the deaths occurred when the workers inhaled gas while inspecting an external nano-filtration tank. Official sources cited in the reports said there were no proper safety measures in place while the effluent treatment plant was being handled. Police have said the final cause of death will be established after the post-mortem, with preliminary findings pointing to toxic gas inhalation.

"We are deeply saddened by the tragic incident that resulted in the deaths of three workers engaged by a sub-contractor of Nalco Water. This incident occurred in a utility facility, operated by Nalco Water. We are working with the local authorities in the investigation of this incident."

— Nalco Water, in a statement reported by Inc42

Investigations Under Way

The deaths will be investigated by Apple, Tata Electronics and local authorities, according to state officials and two sources with direct knowledge of the matter cited by Reuters. An Apple team will visit the plant to assist in the investigation, one source told the news agency. A joint team from the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board and the Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health will also investigate Tata Electronics' role, Financial Express reported.

There was no impact on production, the sources said, because the facility was closed for the Diwali festival this week.

A Plant With a Troubled Recent Record

The Hosur site has faced a series of setbacks. A fire halted production at the components plant in 2024 and injured eleven people. In June this year, the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board warned the unit could be shut down over alleged wastewater contamination of wells in adjacent farmland; Tata Electronics said an independent analysis showed compliance and later said the board had dropped further action. The same month, a ransomware group posted more than two lakh files said to have been stolen from the plant.

Tata's electronics unit accounts for roughly 40 percent of iPhone assembly in India, with Foxconn making up the rest, making the Hosur operation a critical part of Apple's manufacturing base in India, its most important production hub outside China.

What Happens Next

The post-mortem findings will establish the formal cause of death, and the parallel investigations by state agencies, Tata and Apple will determine how the workers came to enter a confined space without the safety measures officials say were missing. The findings will also decide what action follows against the companies responsible for operating and maintaining the treatment plant.
